title: Debug word counter with 3 bugs — 3 turns
description: Word counter has 3 bugs: case sensitivity, punctuation handling, and empty string crash. Fix bugs across turns, then add most_common(n).

files.tests/test_word_counter.py:
import pytest
from word_counter import WordCounter


def test_basic_count():
    wc = WordCounter()
    wc.add_text("hello world hello")
    assert wc.count("hello") == 2
    assert wc.count("world") == 1


def test_case_insensitive():
    wc = WordCounter()
    wc.add_text("Hello HELLO hello")
    assert wc.count("hello") == 3


def test_punctuation_stripped():
    wc = WordCounter()
    wc.add_text("hello, world! hello.")
    assert wc.count("hello") == 2
    assert wc.count("world") == 1


def test_empty_string():
    wc = WordCounter()
    wc.add_text("")
    assert wc.total() == 0


def test_total_count():
    wc = WordCounter()
    wc.add_text("a b c a")
    assert wc.total() == 4


def test_missing_word_returns_zero():
    wc = WordCounter()
    assert wc.count("nothere") == 0


def test_most_common():
    wc = WordCounter()
    wc.add_text("a a a b b c")
    result = wc.most_common(2)
    assert result[0] == ("a", 3)
    assert result[1] == ("b", 2)


def test_most_common_less_than_n():
    wc = WordCounter()
    wc.add_text("hello world")
    result = wc.most_common(10)
    assert len(result) == 2

task_spec.prompt:
The `WordCounter` class in `word_counter.py` has bugs. Read the code carefully — I see at least 3 issues:
1. `add_text` doesn't lowercase words before counting
2. Punctuation is stripped into `cleaned` but the original `word` is stored instead
3. `count()` doesn't lowercase the lookup key
Fix these three bugs. Don't implement `most_common` yet. Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q`.
